les: Party goedere is meer werd as ander
kaps_punt: Waardes van geselekteerde grondstowwe en vervaardigde goedere

items.bewering: 'n Woltrui het by 'n skaap begin, en 'n brood het as koring in 'n saailand begin.
items.bron: Alberta Wool fact sheet 'processing' (alberta.wool.ca) and Maine State Museum 'Wool Production In Depth' (wool is shorn from sheep); LibreTexts Chemistry of Cooking 2.03 'Milling of Wheat' (bread flour is milled from wheat grown as a crop).

items.bewering: Wol, koring en water is dinge wat mense uit die natuur kry.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'definitions field: natural resources'; ISO 59004:2024 (a natural resource is a raw material occurring in nature, usually not yet processed by people). Wool and wheat are farmed, but in geography they count as renewable natural resources and raw materials.

items.bewering: 'n Ding uit die natuur wat mense gebruik, noem ons 'n natuurlike hulpbron.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'definitions field: natural resources'; UN ESCWA sustainable-development glossary 'natural resources' (materials found in nature that people use).

items.bewering: Water is baie meer werd vir iemand wat ver geloop het as vir iemand by 'n kraan.
items.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: Economics Online, 'Exploring the paradox of value' (water is worth far more to a person for whom it is scarce than to one with plenty at hand: marginal utility). The comparison holds: what makes the water worth more is that it is hard to get for that person. A learner who reasons on from it, to the idea that something is worth more where it is scarce, reaches the correct conclusion, and that is exactly what the lesson teaches next.

items.bewering: Waarde is wat iets vir mense werd is. Dit is wat hulle bereid is om daarvoor te gee.
items.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Subjective theory of value' (Menger, Jevons, Walras: the worth people place on a good); Impact Pricing blog, 'Value is not the same as willingness to pay' (willingness to pay as the measure of what something is worth to the buyer). A fair simplification for Grade 6.

items.bewering: 'n Prys is iets anders: dit is wat in geld daarvoor gevra word.
items.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: Impact Pricing blog (price is the amount actually charged, in money or another currency), as against value and willingness to pay.

items.bewering: Die wol in 'n woltrui is dieselfde wol wat op die skaap gegroei het.
items.bron: Alberta Wool fact sheet 'processing'; onlineclothingstudy.com 'Processing of wool fibre' (the fibre is cleaned, carded and spun but stays the same animal fibre; washing removes grease and dirt, not the wool).

items.bewering: Hulle het die skaap geskeer, die wol gewas en gespin en toe 'n trui gebrei.
items.bron: Alberta Wool fact sheet 'processing'; Maine State Museum 'Wool Production In Depth' (shearing, then washing, carding and spinning, then knitting or weaving). The order is right. Carding is left out, which simplifies the list without making it false.

items.bewering: Jy kan daardie werk nie in die trui sien nie. Die werk het van die wol iets gemaak wat mense wil dra. Daarom is die trui meer werd as die wol.
items.bron: superfastcpa.com 'What is Value Added?' and US 1870 census summary (statcan/Wisconsin census summaries): a processed product sells for more than its inputs, and the difference is the value added by manufacture. The reason given is that the work turned the wool into something people want, which ties value to what people want. That fits the lesson's own definition and does not slip into 'value = effort'.

items.bewering: 'n Meule maal die koring tot meel, en 'n bakker bak die brode.
items.bron: LibreTexts Chemistry of Cooking 2.03 'Milling of Wheat'; flourinfo.co.nz 'Flour Milling Process' (mills grind wheat into flour); Suffolk Heritage thesaurus 'stone mill'.

items.bewering: Die brode is meer werd as die koring waarmee alles begin het.
items.bron: fiveable.me 'value added' (principles of macroeconomics) uses exactly the chain wheat to mill to flour to bakery to bread, with value added at each stage, so the bread is worth more than the wheat it came from.

items.bewering: 'n Vervaardigde goed is meestal meer werd as die grondstof waaruit dit gemaak is.
items.bron: US 1870 census summary (raw materials about $2.49 billion, products about $4.23 billion); 1926 Canadian census of manufactures (statcan.gc.ca) and the Wisconsin 1920 census, all reporting a positive 'value added by manufacture'. Because the sentence says 'meestal', it allows for the exceptions where a product is not worth more than its inputs.

items.bewering: Die werk en die kundigheid van mense het van die koring iets gemaak wat mense meer wil hê.
items.bron: superfastcpa.com 'What is Value Added?' (labour and finishing turn inputs into a product that sells for more).

items.bewering: Is daar min van 'n hulpbron en wil baie mense dit hê, dan styg sy waarde. Is daar meer as genoeg daarvan, dan daal sy waarde.
items.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
items.bron: Economics Online 'Exploring the paradox of value' (plentiful goods have low marginal value and scarce goods that people want have high marginal value). The first sentence correctly makes it depend on both scarcity and demand, which avoids the trap of 'rare, therefore valuable'.

items.bewering: Werk laat waarde ook styg wanneer dit 'n grondstof verander in iets wat mense meer wil hê.
items.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
items.bron: superfastcpa.com 'What is Value Added?'; census 'value added by manufacture' data as above. The condition 'iets wat mense meer wil hê' is right: work on its own adds no value if nobody wants what comes out.

items.bewering: 'n Hulpbron wat van ver af moes kom, is meer werd daar waar mense dit gebruik as daar waar dit uitgehaal is.
items.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
items.bron: RIETI Discussion Paper 15-E-017, Kano, Kano and Takechi, 'The Price of Distance' (transport costs are the main source of price differences between regions far apart); Koren via CEPR (goods that cost more to ship show bigger price differences between places). A resource is only carried far if it is worth more where it ends up, so the claim holds for traded resources.

items.bewering: Dieselfde hulpbron kan in die een jaar meer werd wees as in die ander. Was 'n oes swak, dan is daar minder koring en styg die waarde.
items.bron: The Grocer, 'Price of loaf set to rise further as poor harvests force up wheat cost by 50%'; The Manufacturer, 'Wheat prices hit UK' (Russia's drought in 2010, wheat up more than 40% in a month); ITV News, 10 October 2012 (UK wheat yields down 14.1%, price up about 29% year on year).

items.bewering: Waarde is iets wat mense aan 'n hulpbron gee en nie iets wat in die ding sit nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Subjective theory of value'; Market subwiki 'Subjective theory of value' (contrasted with intrinsic theories). This is the mainstream economic position since Menger, Jevons and Walras (1870s). The labour theory of value is the historical alternative. The lesson does not contradict itself here: where it says work raises value, it always adds 'iets wat mense (meer) wil hê'.

items.bewering: natuurlike hulpbron: Iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik, soos water, hout of steenkool.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'definitions field: natural resources'; sathee.iitk.ac.in 'Geography: Natural Resources' (water renewable, coal non-renewable fossil fuel, wood from forests as a biotic resource). The definition matches the study block word for word in substance.

items.bewering: waarde: Wat iets vir mense werd is en wat hulle daarvoor wil gee.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Subjective theory of value'; Impact Pricing blog on value and willingness to pay. Read on its own, the entry is accurate and matches the study block ('bereid is om daarvoor te gee').

opsomming: Every checkable claim in this lesson on value checks out: the steps from sheep to jersey and from wheat to bread, the difference between value and price, scarcity and demand, transport, a poor harvest, and value as something people give a thing rather than something inside it. The lesson contains no superlatives; its one quantifier, 'meestal', is correctly hedged. The water comparison maps soundly onto scarcity, and wherever the lesson says work raises value it ties that to what people want, so it does not quietly teach that effort alone makes something valuable.
